description: We are in elementary school. we hope to create an app that everybody would like and use. This is our first time joining this hackathon. We want to get better at coding.
summary: Mar Exchange is a multiplayer board game designed to introduce players to resource management during Mars exploration. Players roll dice, move between squares named after real Martian craters, and trade power, oxygen, and radiation shield supplies. Simulated space weather adds another challenge: players must decide when to protect their rovers while keeping every resource above zero. Using real NASA Mars imagery, Mar Exchange combines space exploration, strategy, and learning in a browser game. The last rover remaining wins.
details:
Mar Exchange turns the challenge of managing supplies during space exploration into an interactive game for two to four players. Our goal is to make Mars exploration approachable through simple rules, meaningful choices, and real planetary imagery.

Each player controls a different rover and begins at the START square, named after Jezero Crater, with 12 units each of power, oxygen, and radiation shield supplies. Players roll two dice to move around a board containing 24 squares named after real Martian craters. Every square offers two trades involving the three resources. Players must complete one trade before ending their turn, so every move requires a decision about which supplies to spend and which to preserve.

Solar flares and magnetic storms alternate every minute of active play. Players have a short warning period to raise their shields before impact. Raised shields use shield supplies to block a hit, while unprotected rovers lose oxygen or power, depending on the event. Shields can remain raised between turns. If any resource reaches zero, that rover is eliminated. The last surviving rover wins.

Players can create an online room and share an invitation link so friends can join from separate devices. The game also supports playing together on one screen. Additional features include a shared pause button, distinct rover pieces, written instructions, and read-aloud controls. Each Listen button in the instructions reads one paragraph.

The game uses a real orbital image of the Schiaparelli crater region from NASA Mars Trek’s Viking MDIM 2.1 imagery, credited to NASA/JPL/USGS. Crater names come from the USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature. The board’s route, trades, resource values, and space-weather timing are fictional gameplay choices, rather than scientific measurements.

We developed Mar Exchange as a browser game using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with a shared backend for online rooms. We used OpenAI’s Codex AI assistant to help implement, test, and publish the game and prepare the demonstration video. Our aim is to encourage curiosity about Mars while helping players explore how resource shortages and changing conditions affect their decisions. - chatgpt
